slides.title: Nine probes on the test range
slides.text: The last tower is the Test Range. A launcher sends probes out over the red ground, and each one lands a little nearer or farther than the one before. Tally has the landings of nine probes and wants to know two things: what a typical landing is, and how much the landings vary.

slides.title: The middle landing
slides.text: A dot plot puts one dot over the number line for each landing. To find the median, put the nine landings in order and take the middle one: the 5th. Four probes landed at or before it and four at or after it. The median here is 14 meters.
slides.say: A dot plot puts one dot over the number line for each landing. To find the median, put the nine landings in order and take the middle one, the 5th. Four probes landed at or before it and four at or after it. The median here is 14 meters.

visual.label: Nine landings on a dot plot, in meters

focus.cue: The middle landing, the 5th in order, is at 14.

slides.title: The mean and how far landings stray
slides.text: The mean shares the total out equally. The mean absolute deviation, or MAD, is the average distance of the landings from the mean. A small MAD means the landings stay close together.

slides.title: Five numbers make a box plot
slides.text: A box plot shows the lowest landing, the lower quartile, the median, the upper quartile and the highest landing. The box holds the middle half of the data. Its width is the interquartile range: 16 − 11 = 5 meters.

visual.label: Where the probes landed, as a box plot

focus.cue: The box runs from the lower quartile, 11, to the upper quartile, 16.
The line in the box is the median, 14.
The whiskers reach the lowest and highest landings, 8 and 20.

slides.title: Center, spread and shape
slides.text: To describe a set of data, give its center, its spread and its shape. Say how many values there are and what was measured. A landing far from the rest pulls the mean toward it but hardly moves the median, so the median can be the fairer center.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for center and spread.

words.means: the middle value when the data are put in order
the total shared out equally: add the values, then divide by how many there are
the upper quartile minus the lower quartile: how wide the middle half is
the average distance of the values from the mean

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Launch Lab at Spread Test. Find the median and the mean of the landings, pick the more consistent launcher, and read a box plot and a histogram. A wrong plan shows you what it really gives.
slides.alt: Launch Lab on a phone: a data board with a dot plot of nine probe landings in meters, and a stepper to set the median.
